lines.trans: Before we start filming, I have one piece of advice for you: how to use your hands and eyes.
My hands and my eyes?
Hands are the most vital part for expressing a woman's beauty; human emotion shows in the hands.
Stay conscious of your hands so their movement never goes lifeless.

words.gram: Adverbial noun used for strong emphasis.

lines.trans: And whatever happens, never close your eyes — with no script today, your eyes tell the entire story.
My eyes tell the story?
Keep just those two rules, and for everything else act freely just as you feel.
Understood.
Hey mister, got any whistles in this shop? A whistle!
You don't carry any?! Where on earth can a guy find a whistle?!
Hey pops, got a whistle in here? Hurry it up, please!

words.gram: Adverbial く-form of 早い (early) modifying 帰って.
Plain imperative of くれる (give/do for me).

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。

meanings.note: Native Japanese counter for general objects and abstract things like reasons.

examples.text: 理由がもう一つあります。
りんごを一つください。
撮影する前に、君に一つアドバイスしておくことがある。手と目の使い方だ。
examples.trans: Before we start filming, I have one piece of advice for you: how to use your hands and eyes.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

おく.gloss: do in advance; keep in state

meanings.note: After a te-form (積んでおきました, contracted 入っとけ), indicates doing something in advance or staying put.

examples.text: 窓を開けておきました。
ここに置いておきます。
examples.trans: I will leave it here for now.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: Noun.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Godan verb.

examples.text: このペンを使ってもいいですか。
もっと英語を使いましょう。

meanings.en: respectful word for a person (かた)
meanings.note: Read かた, polite replacement for 人 (ひと) when announcing visitors or customers.

examples.text: あの方はどなたですか。

examples.trans: The person in charge has arrived.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Expresses frustration, regret, or surprise that reality contradicts what was expected; often trails off at the end of a spoken complaint.

examples.text: 約束したのに来なかった。
examples.trans: Even though they promised, they did not come.

examples.text: せっかくの休みなのに。
examples.trans: Even though it is a hard-earned day off.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (一番近い), forms the superlative ('closest').

examples.trans: This one is the most popular.

examples.text: 一番近い駅はどこですか。

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Refers to humans in general or human nature.

examples.text: 人間には表と裏がある。
examples.trans: Human beings have a public face and a hidden side.

examples.text: 手は女性を美しく表現するのに一番大切なパーツだ。人間の情感は手に出る。
examples.trans: Hands are the most vital part for expressing a woman's beauty; human emotion shows in the hands.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Adverbial noun used for strong certainty.

examples.text: 明日は絶対に来てください。

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

examples.text: 絶対に手の動きが死なないように意識しろ。
examples.trans: Stay conscious of your hands so their movement never goes lifeless.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.note: Ichidan verb, used for eyes, books, doors, etc.
Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.en: that (near the listener or just mentioned)
meanings.note: Must always precede a noun (その椅子 'that chair').
Used adverbially or as a noun to mean 'everything' or 'all of them'.

examples.text: すべてうまくいきました。

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。
でも、委員会の規制を守らないかぎり作品は出せませんよ。
examples.trans: Even so, unless we abide by the commission's regulations, we won't be able to release the film.

examples.text: そうなんだよ、モザイクの規定は守らねえと。
examples.trans: He's right — we've got no choice except following their mosaic rules.

examples.text: この二つだけ守れば、あとは自由に感じたまま自分でやればいい。
examples.trans: Keep just those two rules, and for everything else act freely just as you feel.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb; takes を or と.

examples.text: 季節の変化を感じます。
examples.trans: I feel the change of seasons.

examples.text: 少し高いと感じるかもしれません。
examples.trans: You may feel it's a little expensive.

meanings.note: Reflexive pronoun pointing back to the person under discussion.

examples.text: 自分の言葉で話します。
examples.trans: I speak in my own words.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Points to the place where the speaker currently stands.

examples.text: ここに座ってください。
目がダメなら耳だ。トシ、笛を買ってきてくれ。
examples.trans: If the eyes are off-limits, we aim for the ears. Toshi, go buy me a whistle.

examples.text: は？笛？もうちょっと説明してくれよ、どんな笛だよ！
examples.trans: Huh?! A whistle?! Give me a little more explanation — what kind of whistle?!
Alright, alright, I get it... a whistle...

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for place.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Adverbial form 早く urges someone to hurry up.

examples.trans: I woke up early in the morning.

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.note: Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
